proof_steps.claim: On the first midpoint stage, $k_1=f(-h/2,0)=0$, so the second-stage state remains $0$. Its time is $-h/2+h/2=0$, where the definition of $f$ gives $k_2=f(0,0)=0$. Thus the method output is $0$.

The displayed piecewise function satisfies $y(0)=0$ and $y'(t)=f(t,y(t))$ for $t<0$ and $t>0$. At $t=0$ its two one-sided derivatives are both $0=f(0,y(0))$, so it is an exact solution there as well. Its value at $h/2$ is $h^2/8$, hence the local defect is $0-h^2/8=-h^2/8$.

If one constant $C$ gave the uniform order-two estimate in [F3], these admitted exact-start steps would satisfy $h^2/8\le Ch^3$, hence $1/(8h)\le C$ for every $h>0$. The left side is unbounded as $h\downarrow0$, so no such uniform constant exists. The field is continuous but not differentiable in time at $0$, identifying the missing smoothness condition.
